newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS SIGN LAPOINTE TO FOUR-YEAR DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RED WINGS SIGN LAPOINTE TO FOUR-YEAR DEAL.

text.p: The Detroit Red Wings took their first step towards keeping their Stanley Cup champion nucleus intact by re-signing restricted free agent right winger Martin Lapointe on Wednesday to a four-year contract.

Lapointe, 23, was an instrumental part of the Red Wings' first Stanley Cup in 42 years. He established career highs of 16 goals and 17 assists in the regular season, then stepped it up in the playoffs with four goals and eight assists in 20 games.

"Martin showed marked improvement in his development as a player this season, followed by a tremendous playoffs," said Detroit assistant general manager Ken Holland. "We feel he can use this year's playoffs as a building block for the future."
Lapointe was the 10th overall pick in the 1991 Entry Draft.

With the signing of Lapointe, Detroit has two restricted free agents still to sign -- centre Sergei Fedorov and winger Vyacheslav Kozlov. The Red Wings also have five unrestricted free agents, chief among them winger Igor Larionov.
